GDP.pdf retains 100 expert-authored question/PDF tasks across ten professional domains after at least two frontier models make material errors. Strict pass requires every criterion, while mean rubric score gives partial credit.

repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2607.11192.method

  • This is a source-specific, first-party description; this repair does not independently reproduce experiments or audit operational execution and customer outcomes.
  • Working professionals submit original PDFs, questions and reference answers. Experts write atomic rubric criteria and sanity-check good/bad outputs; retention requires major errors from at least two frontier models.
  • Gemini 3.5 Flash judges criteria separately without source PDF or gold answer and is calibrated to expert raters according to the authors. Discussed failures are hand-checked; the judge family also appears among evaluated models.
  • One hundred selected items span ten domains. Each item is run five times per model with native provider PDF input and no tools/additional context; provider document handling is part of the measured protocol.
  • Table 6 is a July 2026 seventeen-model snapshot. The authors distinguish adversarially selected task performance from professional document work at large; the live leaderboard evolves.
  • Table 2 declares the released benchmark Apache 2.0 while third-party PDFs retain original rights; benchmark licensing is not blanket PDF redistribution permission.
  • This author did not independently audit judge calibration, individual items or underlying PDF rights and does not infer unsupervised-use readiness.

Headline DeepSWE and Terminal-Bench 2.1 baselines are public scores, whereas other baselines are in-house; DeepSWE’s in-house base differs from its public baseline. repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2610.00890.limitation

  • This is a source-specific, first-party description; this repair does not independently reproduce experiments or audit operational execution and customer outcomes.
  • Experts author 1,000 repository-change tasks and 700 terminal tasks. RL is used without a supervised stage; regression tests gate repository reward, while terminal tasks have no pass-to-pass gate.
  • Partial credit is over equally weighted checks/verifier criteria, not necessarily one vote per semantic requirement; a requirement can map to one or more checks.
  • Headline DeepSWE and Terminal-Bench 2.1 baselines are public scores. The in-house DeepSWE baseline differs; Terminal-Bench 2.1 has no in-house base run, and its public baseline averages three runs.
  • Terminal-Bench 4 revises Terminal-Bench 3 and forms one family for pooled analysis. Eight trained Terminal-Bench 3 runs were excluded for harness failures, leaving eight passes among 66 scored runs.
  • The report uses one final trained checkpoint/run. Paired behavioral examples focus on newly solved tasks and do not isolate causal effects of each task or reward property.
